title: Valid Parentheses
summary: Check whether every bracket is closed by the right type, in the right order.
statement:
Given a string `s` containing only the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`, return `true`
if the brackets are valid:

1. Every opening bracket is closed by a bracket of the same type.
2. Brackets are closed in the correct order (innermost first).
3. Every closing bracket has a matching opening bracket.

An empty string is valid.

examples.explanation: The ] closes before the ) that was opened after the [.

hints: When you meet a closing bracket, which opening bracket must it match: the first one you saw, or the most recent one still open?
Most-recent-first is a stack (last in, first out). Push openings; on a closing bracket, pop and check that the types match.

stack = empty
for c in s:
    if c is an opening bracket: push c
    else:
        if stack is empty: return false
        if pop() does not match c: return false
return stack is empty

Brackets nest, so the bracket that has to close next is always the most recently opened one, which is exactly what a stack gives you. Use ArrayDeque<Character> rather than the legacy Stack class. Two edge cases catch people out: a closing bracket when the stack is empty (")(" ), and leftover openings at the end ("(("), which is why the final check is `stack.isEmpty()` rather than `true`. O(n) time and O(n) space.
